post.description:
Create a segment — returns immediately (202).

The body is the full segment definition; the workflow creates it in the
Segments Manager, and the segment is Available as soon as the run
completes. Semantic validation (site, CIDR, overlap, VLAN) belongs to the
Segments Manager, so an invalid definition surfaces as a FAILED workflow on
GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id}, not as a 4xx here — this route only
rejects a body that does not fit InitializeSegmentRequest at all.

The definition carries no type: a segment gets one only when
allocate-segment reserves it. Re-POSTing a definition for a segment that
already exists is harmless (the activity is idempotent); doing so while its
run is still going gets a 409 on the dedup id.

Start one workflow per segment definition — returns immediately (202).

Always 202 with a per-item report, never a single pass/fail status: the
fan-out is partial by nature (some runs start, some are already running,
some are rejected by Temporal), and collapsing that into one status code
would hide which segments actually got a workflow. Duplicate CIDRs within
one request collapse onto the same deterministic workflow id, so the
second occurrence reports `already_running`.

Allocate a VLAN segment for a hosted cluster — returns immediately (202).

The body names the CLUSTER, the SITE to allocate at (the day1 folder the
cluster file goes in, as the Segments Manager spells it) and the TYPE to
allocate it as (default HC). The segment is whichever Available one the
Segments Manager reserves at the site — it becomes that type in the same
step — and the run completes once the allocation reads back verified.
Nothing is written to git: provision-cluster (which starts this run as a
child) records the allocation in the cluster file it publishes, and the
DHCP scope follows when a human merges that file to main. Poll
GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} for progress/result; an unknown site, a
bad cluster name or an exhausted pool surfaces there as a FAILED run, not
as a 4xx here. `values_branch`, the branch the run used to push to, is a
422 saying what replaced it.

Give a decommissioned cluster's segment back to the pool — returns
immediately (202).

Call it only AFTER the cluster's Argo CD Application and everything it
managed are gone: the run deletes the cluster's DHCP scope if it is still
there, and a Crossplane Request that still exists would re-create it. The
hostedcluster-setup chart's PostDelete hook calls this route at exactly
that point (a 409 means a run for the cluster is already going, which the
hook treats as success).

The body names the CLUSTER and the TYPE (default HC); the segment is
looked up in the Segments Manager. A cluster holding no such segment
COMPLETES as a no-op (released=false) rather than failing, so a repeated
trigger is harmless. Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} for
progress/result.

This API has no auth of its own (CLAUDE.md §9), and this route ends in a
DHCP scope DELETE and a segment release.

Install servers into an InfraEnv — returns immediately (202).

The body names the INFRAENV to fill and the MCE cluster it belongs to. The
InfraEnv's name states which hardware it is for
(`cisco-m6-bat-yam-64c-512gb` — vendor, model, site, cores, memory), so it
also selects the servers: the healthy, unclaimed machines server-scan lists
under that name. The VLAN is not an input: it is read from the MCE's own
inventory segment in the Segments Manager.

EVERY SERVER IS ITS OWN WORKFLOW RUN, with its own id, status and failure;
there is never one run for a batch. The body decides how many:

- **Neither `count` nor `server_names`**: the pool picks ONE server, in
  the first free slot (`add-server-to-mce-<mce>_<infraEnv>_<slot>`), answered with
  `{workflow_id, run_id}`. Slots still running are stepped over, so the
  same request sent again while it installs starts a SECOND install — it
  is never a 409 (only when all 100 slots are busy).
- **`count: N`**: the pool picks N, installed IN PARALLEL, one per free
  slot, answered with a per-run report. A second request adds N more.
- **`server_names: "<name>"`**: that one machine
  (`add-server-to-mce-<mce>_<server>`), answered with `{workflow_id, run_id}`;
  a 409 while it is already installing.
- **`server_names: [...]`**: each named machine in parallel, answered with
  a per-run report — always, even for a list of one — in which a machine
  already installing is `already_running`.

Runs cannot take the same machine, whichever way they were asked for: each
takes server-scan's install lock (an atomic compare-and-set there) before
writing anything, and server-scan stops listing a locked machine. A pool
run that loses the race skips to its next candidate, and one left with
none fails with ServerReservedError — raise `candidate_count`, or the pool
has fewer free servers than are being installed. A named machine another
run took first fails its own run.

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} (one per run) for progress/result.
No healthy server matching, no candidate with two link-up NICs on distinct
physical ports, or a BareMetalHost that never registers all surface there
as a FAILED run — not as a 4xx here.

post.description:
Take one server out of an MCE's inventory — returns immediately (202).

Deletes the server's Agent, its BareMetalHost (`<server>`) and its
NMStateConfig (`nmstate-config-<server>`) after powering the host off.
Only for a server that is just inventory: if its Agent is bound to a
cluster the run FAILS having changed nothing (`AgentBoundToClusterError`).
A server with nothing on the MCE completes as a no-op (`found: false`).

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} for progress/result. One removal
per server at a time: a second trigger while one runs gets a 409.

Take servers all the way out of an MCE — returns immediately (202).

Whatever state each server is in. A hosted cluster's node first leaves the
hosted cluster — its CAPI Machine is deleted, CAPI drains the Node, the
Agent provider unbinds the Agent — and then, like a host that was only
inventory, leaves the MCE through remove-server-from-mce, run as the uninstall's
child (`remove-server-from-mce-<server>`).

**Nothing has to be done first: the run deletes the node's Machine itself.**
NodePool replicas are never touched, so the NodePool backfills a new
Machine from another free Agent it matches — the node is REPLACED, the
cluster keeps its size. If this server is the only free Agent, the
replacement takes it back and the run stops (AgentRetakenError) without
writing anything more.

Every uninstall ends there: there is no option to keep the server in the
MCE's inventory (`keep_inventory` was removed on 2026-11-02 and is a 422).

The reply follows what was sent: one name is `{workflow_id, run_id}` on
`uninstall-server-from-hc-<server>` and a 409 while that server is uninstalling;
a list (1-20, each once) is a per-run report, even for a list of one.

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} (one per server) for progress and
result. server-scan disagreeing with the MCE, an Agent bound with no
AgentMachine, a lock another run holds, a drain stuck for 20 minutes or an
orphaned Node all surface there as a FAILED run — not as a 4xx here.

schema.title: Response Start Uninstall Server From Hc Workflows Server Lifecycle Uninstall Server From Hc Post

post.summary: Start Publish Infraenv To Pxe Server
post.description:
Put an InfraEnv's current iPXE script on its site's PXE VM — returns immediately (202).

Writes `/var/www/pxe-map/<mce_cluster>/<infra_env>.ipxe` on the PXE VM of
the MCE's inventory-segment site: the boot entry every IPMI host mapped to
the InfraEnv chains to. Waits (bounded, 10 min) for the InfraEnv to have a
ready discovery image; a VM already holding a newer image keeps it, and
the run completes as `superseded`.

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} for progress/result. One publish per
(MCE, InfraEnv) at a time: a second trigger while one runs gets a 409.

Provision one Dell server from its iDRAC IP — returns immediately (202).

The run discovers the server in OpenManage, deploys the template for its
model and iDRAC firmware (which sets root's password), builds the RAID 1 on
the BOSS and sets every PERC drive Non-RAID, has the naming service rename
its profile, and completes once the machine is configured: root on the
enforced password, the template applied, the storage layout verified and
the OME profile carrying the right name. It does NOT wait for server-scan
to list the machine — server-scan's own collector finds it on its next
pass (every 6 h), which is well after this run has finished.

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id}; its `progress.phase` and
`progress.waiting_on` say where the run is. A second POST for the same IP
while a run is going gets a 409.

Provision many Dell servers — one workflow per iDRAC IP (202).

Always 202 with a per-item report: some start, some are already running,
some are rejected (no region for their prefix) — one bad row never holds
the others back. A repeated IP in one request reports `already_running`.

Start upgrading one HostedCluster — returns immediately (202).

The run plans the path, pins every release to a digest, runs the
pre-flight, and waits for `approve` with nothing committed. Poll
GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id}: its `progress.waiting_for` says what is
needed next. One run per cluster: a second start while one runs is a 409.

get.description:
What one cluster can be upgraded to: the "New upgrade" form's choices (D22).

Every ladder rung newer than the cluster's mastertag, of a minor its MCE
supports, to which a path resolves, newest first. SYNCHRONOUS, unlike every
other route here: read from day1 git by a short upgrade-targets run, waited
for up to 60 s. 404 when day1 has no such cluster, 409 when its file or
rules cannot be used, 504 when nothing answered.

parameters.name: cluster

schema.description: The day1 cluster file's name (also its Argo CD Application), without `.yaml`. Not the HostedCluster's name, which the chart derives from the file.
schema.title: Cluster

parameters.description: The day1 cluster file's name (also its Argo CD Application), without `.yaml`. Not the HostedCluster's name, which the chart derives from the file.

post.description: The one approval, before anything is committed. Only while the run waits for it.

Give the admin acks a control-plane minor step needs although clients still call the APIs
they remove (listed in the run's `waiting_for`). Only while the run waits for it; `retry`
instead checks the callers again.
Roll the next NodePool (manual mode) — optionally naming which. Only while one waits.
The day2 layer for the control plane's new version is synced: carry on.
Hold the run before its next commit. What is already rolling finishes.
Carry on from where a `pause` held the run. Only while it is paused.

Stop. Before approval the run is CANCELLED, nothing committed. After it, the run
commits `pausedUntil` for the HostedCluster and every NodePool and syncs: ABORTED.
Nothing is ever rolled back — there is no downgrade.

Re-run what failed. Only while the run waits for a person (needs-human), or for an
admin-ack approval, where it checks the API callers again.
Run one action the agent proposed, with the workflow's identity. Then `retry`.
Refuse one action the agent proposed: it is recorded and never run. Then `retry` or `abort`.

Create VirtualMachines for a KubeVirt InfraEnv — returns immediately (202).

EVERY VM IS ITS OWN RUN on a slot of the InfraEnv on its MCE
(`create-vm-<mce>_<infraEnv>_<slot>`), because the VM's name is drawn
inside the run. Without `count`: one run, in the first free slot, answered
with `{workflow_id, run_id}` — asking again while it runs starts a SECOND
VM, never a 409 (only when all 100 slots are busy). With `count: N`: N runs
in parallel, one per free slot, answered with a per-run report.

Each run lists the zone's KubeVirt clusters from the day1 repo, reads
every one's capacity, picks the best-fitting cluster under the headroom
buffer, creates ONE Halted VM with a fixed MAC there and waits (bounded,
10 min) for its root disk to bind. Nothing fitting, or a disk that never
binds (the VM is deleted again), is a FAILED run — not a 4xx here.

Poll GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id} (one per run) for progress/result;
the result carries the VM's name and MAC, the cluster and the ranking table.

post.description:
Provision a hosted cluster from its YAML — returns immediately (202).

The BODY is the cluster file (`Content-Type: application/yaml`; "Try it
out" shows the slim shape to edit). `cluster` and `mce` are query
parameters. The run reads day1 main for the MCE folder, judges the file
against the value layers, allocates a segment (allocate-segment, as a
child), pushes the file with the allocation block to
`provision-cluster/<cluster>`, opens the merge request and WAITS for a
person to merge it — no deadline — then registers the cluster in the day2
sig repos the value layers list, and completes. A rejected file, an
unknown MCE folder, a cluster already in day1 or a closed merge request
is a FAILED run on GET /workflows/runs/{workflow_id}, not a 4xx here; a
second request for the same cluster while its run waits is a 409.

This API has no auth of its own (CLAUDE.md §9): this route pushes a
branch and opens a merge request on the day1 repo.

parameters.name: cluster

schema.description: The hosted cluster's name, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix — `prep-e2e-site2-a` and `ocp4-prep-e2e-site2-a` name the same cluster. It becomes the day1 file `ocp4-<name>.yaml`, the Argo CD Application and the Segments Manager's cluster. A lowercase DNS-1123 label of at most 24 characters.

parameters.description: The hosted cluster's name, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix — `prep-e2e-site2-a` and `ocp4-prep-e2e-site2-a` name the same cluster. It becomes the day1 file `ocp4-<name>.yaml`, the Argo CD Application and the Segments Manager's cluster. A lowercase DNS-1123 label of at most 24 characters.

schema.description: The MCE FOLDER the cluster goes in, exactly as named under day1's `sites/<site>/mces/` (`ocp4-prep-mce-site2-a`, `ocp4-mce-site2`). The site is read from where the folder is.

requestBody.description: The hosted-cluster YAML file, as a person would commit it to day1 — WITHOUT vlanId, dhcp_values or mcConfigMap: the run appends the allocation, the day1 CI chain the MachineConfigs. Sent verbatim; comments and layout reach day1 unchanged.

owner:
  merkaz: "unit-a"
  anaf: "unit-b"
  mador: "unit-c"

mastertag: 4.22.8

nodepool:
- infraEnvName: dell-r660-site4-128c-1024gb-5tb
  replicas: 2
  labels:
    allowDeletion: false
  configs:
  - name: nm-conf
  - name: worker-kubeletconfig-reserved
  - name: nic-ring-buffer
  - name: workers-chrony-configuration

schema.title: Response List Workflow Runs Workflows Runs Get

get.description: Status of any workflow run: state, live progress, final result.

by.title: By
by.description: Who decides; recorded in the run's log.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why; an abort is never anonymous or unexplained.

by.title: By
by.description: Who decides on the action; recorded in the run's log.

ActionDecisionRequest.title: ActionDecisionRequest
ActionDecisionRequest.description: The body of an agent proposal's approve or reject; the action is named in the path.

AddServerToMceBatchResponse.title: AddServerToMceBatchResponse
AddServerToMceBatchResponse.description:
The answer to `count` or a `server_names` list: one item per run.

Always 202 with a per-run report, never one pass/fail code: starting
several runs is partial by nature (some start, some are already running,
Temporal may refuse one), and one status code would hide which got a run.

For `count`, `results` lists every slot looked at, in order: the busy ones
stepped over, the ones started, and a `failed` start if any. `started` <
`count` means not enough free slots were found, or a start failed (the
scan stops there rather than failing slot after slot). For a list of
names, one item per name, in order; a refused name does not stop the rest.

AddServerToMceItem.title: AddServerToMceItem
AddServerToMceItem.description:
One install of a multi-server request.

`server_name` for a named server; `slot` for a pool run, whose machine the
run itself picks (its progress and result name it).

infra_env.title: Infra Env
infra_env.description: The InfraEnv to fill. Its name states the hardware (`cisco-m6-bat-yam-64c-512gb`), so it is also the pool: the healthy, unclaimed servers server-scan lists as `ocp-<infra_env>…`.

mce_cluster.title: Mce Cluster
mce_cluster.description: The target MCE, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix: `prod-mce-bat-yam` and `ocp4-prod-mce-bat-yam` name the same cluster, and the run always uses the prefixed name.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace of the InfraEnv on the MCE, where the BareMetalHost, its Secret and NMStateConfig are created. Defaults to `inventory`.

server_names.title: Server Names
server_names.description: Install exactly these machines (server-scan names) instead of letting the pool pick: one name, or a list of up to 20, each once. Each is its own run. Not with `count` or `candidate_count`.

count.title: Count
count.description: Let the pool pick this many healthy servers and install them IN PARALLEL, one run each. Omitted, the pool picks one. Runs already going on the pool are stepped over, so asking again — with or without `count` — adds installs rather than colliding.

candidate_count.title: Candidate Count
candidate_count.description: How many healthy servers each pool run asks server-scan for, so it has others to try when one is unusable or another run takes it. Defaults to one per run on the pool plus 2 (at most 20): 3 for a lone install.

AddServerToMceRequest.title: AddServerToMceRequest
AddServerToMceRequest.description:
The add-server-to-mce request body: one shape for every way of asking.

Which servers: with none named, the InfraEnv's pool picks `count` healthy
ones (1 unless sent); `server_names` names the machines instead, one or a
list. Either way every server is a run of its own (`run_input`).

Deliberately NOT AddServerToMceInput, nor a subclass of it: a request is no
longer one run. That model is decoded from Temporal history on every
replay, so it keeps its shape (`server_name` singular, no `count`) and the
strictness lives here, at the edge, instead — chiefly a `vlan_id` is
refused: the VLAN belongs to the MCE's inventory segment, so a caller
supplying one expects it to be used, and ignoring it would tag the host
with a different VLAN than was asked for.

by.title: By
by.description: Who decides; recorded in the run's log.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the clients the run listed may lose the API this ack lets the upgrade remove (they moved off it, or they may break). Recorded in the run's log.

AllocateSegmentRequest.title: AllocateSegmentRequest
AllocateSegmentRequest.description:
The allocate-segment request body: AllocateSegmentInput with the site
REQUIRED, the retired `values_branch` refused, and unknown fields refused.

`site` is required HERE, not on AllocateSegmentInput: that model is
decoded from Temporal history on every replay, and a run started before
the field existed carries none — a required field there would fail to
decode it and wedge the run. At the edge, a caller omitting it gets a 422
now instead of a run that fails SiteMissingError later. It is held to the
naming convention's token shape (lowercase letters, digits, single dashes),
which is also what a day1 folder name is.

`values_branch` was the day1 branch the run pushed the allocation block to
(until 2026-11-11). provision-cluster owns the cluster file now, so a
caller still sending it expects a push that will not happen: refused with
a 422 saying what replaced it, never silently ignored.

`extra="forbid"` refuses a misspelt field (`branch`, `cluster_name`)
instead of silently allocating as if it had not been sent.

BulkInitializeSegmentInput.title: BulkInitializeSegmentInput
BulkInitializeSegmentInput.description:
Many segment definitions in one request (e.g. a CSV import).

Fans out to one workflow PER SEGMENT rather than one workflow for the
batch: each segment gets its own deterministic id (natural dedup), its own
run status and its own failure — a bad definition in row 7 must not hold up
or fail row 8, and a batch-shaped workflow could offer none of that.

BulkInitializeSegmentItem.title: BulkInitializeSegmentItem
BulkInitializeSegmentItem.description:
Per-segment outcome of the FAN-OUT only — not of the workflow, which by
definition has barely begun. `started` means Temporal accepted the run.

BulkProvisionDellServerItem.title: BulkProvisionDellServerItem
BulkProvisionDellServerItem.description: Per-machine outcome of the FAN-OUT only; the run itself has barely begun.

by.title: By
by.description: Who signs off; recorded in the run's log.

nodepool.title: Nodepool
nodepool.description: Which NodePool rolls next. Default: the next in the run's order.

ContinueRequest.title: ContinueRequest
ContinueRequest.description: The body of continue: the customer's sign-off that their readiness checks passed.

CreateVmBatchResponse.title: CreateVmBatchResponse
CreateVmBatchResponse.description:
The answer to `count`: one item per slot looked at, in order — the busy ones
stepped over, the ones started, a `failed` start if any (the scan stops there).
Always 202 with the report, never one pass/fail code.

mce_cluster.title: Mce Cluster
mce_cluster.description: The MCE whose InfraEnv the VM is for, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix — `prod-mce-bat-yam-a` and `ocp4-prod-mce-bat-yam-a` name the same cluster. Must be named `ocp4-<env>-mce-<site>-<letter>`: the site is read from it.

infra_env.title: Infra Env
infra_env.description: A KubeVirt InfraEnv, `<conf>[-<letter>]-zone-<zone>-<cpu>` (`x201-zone-a-8`): the zone picks the KubeVirt clusters, the number the VM's vCPUs (memory is cpu × 8 GiB). A `-metal` InfraEnv has servers, not VMs, and is refused.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: The VM's namespace on the KubeVirt cluster — the InfraEnv's namespace on the MCE, verbatim; must exist there as a kubevirt-redfish chassis namespace. Defaults to `inventory`.

count.title: Count
count.description: Create this many VMs, one run per free slot, answered with a per-run report; at most 20. Without it: one run, `{workflow_id, run_id}`.

CreateVmRequest.title: CreateVmRequest
CreateVmRequest.description:
The create-vm request body: ONE shape, one or `count` runs.

Its own model, not a CreateVmInput subclass: one request is many runs,
and the run's input carries what the edge derives (`run_input`).

Day1NodePool.title: Day1NodePool
Day1NodePool.description: One `nodepool[]` entry of a day1 cluster file, as written (not as rendered).

by.title: By
by.description: Who decides; recorded in the run's log.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why, optionally; recorded in the run's log.

DecisionRequest.title: DecisionRequest
DecisionRequest.description: The body of approve, confirm-day2, pause, resume and retry: who decides, and optionally why.

DecisionResponse.title: DecisionResponse
DecisionResponse.description: 200 to a decision: the run took it. What it does next shows in its progress.

InitializeSegmentRequest.title: InitializeSegmentRequest
InitializeSegmentRequest.description:
The initialize-segment request body: InitializeSegmentInput, refusing
unknown fields.

Chiefly a `type`: a segment is born typeless and allocate-segment stamps
the type on, so a caller still sending one expects it to mean something.
Ignoring it would create the segment and silently drop what they asked
for; the Segments Manager rejects it on create for the same reason.

The strictness lives HERE, at the edge, not on InitializeSegmentInput:
that model is decoded from Temporal history on every replay and from every
scheduled activity input, and a run started before the type was removed
carries one in its payload — a forbidding model would fail to decode it
and wedge the run.

NodePoolMode.title: NodePoolMode
NodePoolMode.description: Who starts each NodePool roll: a person (`continue`), or the run after a soak.

ProvisionDellServerRequest.title: ProvisionDellServerRequest
ProvisionDellServerRequest.description:
The provision-dell-server request body: one iDRAC IP, unknown fields refused.

The IP is normalized here (`010.001.002.003` is refused, not reinterpreted)
so the workflow id — the dedup key — is the same however it was typed.

mce_cluster.title: Mce Cluster
mce_cluster.description: The target MCE, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix: `prod-mce-bat-yam` and `ocp4-prod-mce-bat-yam` name the same cluster, and the run always uses the prefixed name.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace of the InfraEnv on the MCE. Defaults to `inventory`.

PublishInfraEnvToPxeServerRequest.title: PublishInfraEnvToPxeServerRequest
PublishInfraEnvToPxeServerRequest.description: The publish-infraenv-to-pxe-server request body: strict at the edge, namespace defaulted here.

ReleaseSegmentRequest.title: ReleaseSegmentRequest
ReleaseSegmentRequest.description:
The release-segment request body: ReleaseSegmentInput, refusing
unknown fields.

Release is keyed by CLUSTER (+ type): the segment's CIDR, site and vlan
come from the Segments Manager, so a caller sending `segment` or `site`
expects it to narrow something it does not — refused here instead of
silently ignored. The strictness lives at the edge, never on
ReleaseSegmentInput, which is decoded from Temporal history.

mce_cluster.title: Mce Cluster
mce_cluster.description: The target MCE, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix: `prod-mce-bat-yam` and `ocp4-prod-mce-bat-yam` name the same cluster, and the run always uses the prefixed name.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace of the server's BareMetalHost, NMStateConfig and Agent on the MCE. Defaults to `inventory`.

RemoveServerFromMceRequest.title: RemoveServerFromMceRequest
RemoveServerFromMceRequest.description: The remove-server-from-mce request body: strict at the edge, namespace defaulted here.

SegmentType.title: SegmentType
SegmentType.description:
Segment types known to the Segments Manager.

A type is ALLOCATION state, not part of a segment's definition: a segment
is created with none, the Segments Manager stamps the requested type on
when allocate-segment reserves it, and release clears it again. So the type
appears only on the allocation path (AllocateSegmentInput and what follows
from it), never on initialize-segment's input. (It used to be fixed at
creation, which is why there was once a convert-segment workflow to re-type
Available segments between pools. There are no per-type pools any more, so
there is nothing to convert.)

ServerRunItem.title: ServerRunItem
ServerRunItem.description:
One run of a multi-server request: its START only — the run has barely begun.

The shape every per-server report in this domain shares: add-server-to-mce's
and uninstall-server-from-hc's alike, so a caller reads one the way it reads the
other.

SlotStart.title: SlotStart
SlotStart.description:
One slot a pool request looked at, for a per-run report (workflow_domains/routers/slots.py).

`started`: a new run on `workflow_id` (`run_id` set); `already_running`: the
slot's run is still going and was stepped over; `failed`: Temporal refused
the start (`error`), which ends the scan.

StartWorkflowResponse.title: StartWorkflowResponse

UninstallServerFromHcBatchResponse.title: UninstallServerFromHcBatchResponse
UninstallServerFromHcBatchResponse.description:
The answer to a `server_names` list: one item per server, in order.

Always 202 with a per-run report (see AddServerToMceBatchResponse); a name
already uninstalling is `already_running`, and a refused one does not stop
the rest.

server_names.title: Server Names
server_names.description: The machines to uninstall (server-scan names): one name, or a list of up to 20, each once. Each is its own run.

mce_cluster.title: Mce Cluster
mce_cluster.description: The target MCE, with or without its `ocp4-` prefix: `prod-mce-bat-yam` and `ocp4-prod-mce-bat-yam` name the same cluster, and the run always uses the prefixed name. Needed because it names the activity queue of the worker inside that MCE.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Namespace of the server's BareMetalHost and Agent on the MCE (the InfraEnv's). Defaults to `inventory`.

UninstallServerFromHcRequest.title: UninstallServerFromHcRequest
UninstallServerFromHcRequest.description:
The uninstall-server-from-hc request body: which machines, on which MCE.

`server_names` ONLY — no cluster, NodePool or HostedCluster field, and no
`count`: server-scan and each Agent's own binding say where a server is,
and a caller-supplied cluster could only contradict them. Its OWN model,
not an UninstallServerFromHcInput subclass, for add-server-to-mce's reason: one
request is many runs, each built by `run_input` with ONE `server_name`.

cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.description: The day1 cluster file's name (also its Argo CD Application), without `.yaml`. Not the HostedCluster's name, which the chart derives from the file. The run finds the hosting MCE from where that file is, `sites/<site>/mces/<mce>/hostedClusters/<cluster>.yaml`.

target_version.title: Target Version
target_version.description: The release to end on, `X.Y.Z` (or `X.Y.Z-x86_64`). Must be in the mirror.

target_minor.title: Target Minor
target_minor.description: Instead of `target_version`: a minor, `4.21`. The run picks the newest release of it that is both mirrored and a ladder rung.

nodepool_mode.description: Who starts each NodePool roll. `manual` (default): the run waits for `continue` before every NodePool, the customer's sign-off after their own readiness checks. `auto`: the next NodePool rolls once the previous one's gate has held for the soak, and nobody is asked. `auto` only for a cluster file with `upgrade.wave` 0 or 1 (lab, canary), else planning fails.

nodepool_order.title: Nodepool Order
nodepool_order.description: The order NodePools roll in; each exactly once. Default: the cluster file's `upgrade.nodePoolOrder`, else by zone, else file order.

max_unavailable.title: Max Unavailable
max_unavailable.description: Per NodePool, how many of its nodes an InPlace roll takes down at once: a whole number (1 or more) or a percentage (`"33%"`, 1% to 100%), e.g. `{"zone-a": 2}`. The run writes it into the cluster file's `nodepool[].inPlace.maxUnavailable` in the same commit as that NodePool's workertag, and it stays there after the upgrade. A NodePool not named keeps the file's own. Each name must be a NodePool this plan rolls, else planning fails.

workers_to_target.title: Workers To Target
workers_to_target.description: `true` (default): the plan ends with every NodePool at the target. `false`: control plane only; a NodePool moves only where the path forces it (more than `maxWorkerSkew` minors behind, or a `dataPlane: required` rung).

auto_approve.title: Auto Approve
auto_approve.description: `true`: the run approves its own plan after pre-flight instead of waiting for `approve`. Only for a cluster file with `upgrade.wave` 0 or 1 (lab, canary), else planning fails. `confirm-day2`, an admin ack a client still needs, every needs-human stop and every agent proposal still wait for a person.

requested_by.title: Requested By
requested_by.description: Who asked; recorded in the run's log.

UpgradeClusterRequest.title: UpgradeClusterRequest
UpgradeClusterRequest.description: The upgrade-cluster request body: strict at the edge, normalised before the run sees it.

UpgradeTarget.title: UpgradeTarget
UpgradeTarget.description: One release a person may pick as an upgrade target (the "New upgrade" form's dropdown).

UpgradeTargets.title: UpgradeTargets
UpgradeTargets.description:
What a cluster can be upgraded to, read from day1 git (DESIGN §4, D22).

Every ladder rung newer than the control plane whose minor the hosting
MCE supports and to which a path resolves, newest first. The ladder is what
the team mirrored and verified, so a minor missing from the internal
registry is never offered. From git, so it is intent: planning still checks
git against the cluster and pins every release in the mirror.
